questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Several aspects played a role in the destination I chose. LMU is a high ranked university in Europe, which definitely entered my mind when making my decision. In addition, I know a few people in the city which help make up my mind. Geographically Munich is located such that it allows for a plethora of weekend trips e.g. skiing during winter season or hiking when the weather allows it.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The university and support groups set up for a great exchange semester. Unfortunately, the pandemic did play quite a large role as the semester went on and in the second half of the semester all classes were online.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: All necessary information was more or less readily available online or through supplied information by email.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: A welcome meeting (on zoom, however) was arranged before the semester started. This allowed for all exchange students to ask questions if necessary and to some extent meet each other. A whatass group was created and shared in the chat during the zoom meeting.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I was lucky getting housing, since I was able to get a room with a friend of mine. However, by speaking to others getting (affordable) housing was not particularly easy. I also tried signing up for exchange student dorms but was unsuccessful - very few rooms are available.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Be prepared to pay similar prices to Copenhagen. Typically in a shared flat one can easily end up paying €700-1000. Try your luck online e.g. in Facebook groups for exchange students, but be wary of scammers and offers that sound too good to be true.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The entire process is detailed through email and is fairly straight forward. Just keep an eye on your KU-mail and everything should be self-explanatory.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: If you have any questions an email-address is stated in the enrollment email.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was able to register for all classes/seminars I wanted to.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
The course catalogue is not available since fairly close to the semester's starting date, so do not get your heart set on any courses that have previously been taught. You do not actually sign up for courses, rather you sign up for the exam and simply add the course to your schedule on the online platform. As such, you are able to "shop around" for courses and try a few before deciding for which courses you will attend the exam.

I would recommend signing up for one or two courses with exams at the end up the first "block" of the semester, such that all your exams are not crammed together within a couple of weeks at the end of the semester.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I would argue that the academic level was fairly similar to what you would experience at UCPH.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The teaching style is also very similar to UCPH. You attend the course through the semester but are simply graded on the final exam. Most courses are split into lectures and tutorials - make sure you attend the tutorials.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Managerial Economics 1
SPS "Taxation and Regulation of the Financial WiSe 2122 Sector" (Seminar)
Frontiers in International Trade
The Economics of Power Markets

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend signing up for a seminar - the writing period is 4 weeks and if scheduled correctly can take the ease off a potentially stressful exam period. Frontiers in International Trade was a particularly enjoyable course on advanced international trade - if you have any experience with international trade courses and/or want to write a thesis within the field, the two professors do a great job presenting newer research (including their own) within the field.

questions.answer: Enrollment at the university of €144.4

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Munich is a fairly expensive city by German standard - especially eating at restaurants / going out is more expensive that e.g. Berlin. Groceries, on the other hand, were cheaper than expected (compared to CPH).

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Join the ESN Mesa group - they offer lots of trips, daily activities etc. A great way to meet fellow exchange students. I assume the pandemic unfortunately played a significant role particularly w.r.t. athletic activities.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: As mentioned, try to participate in as many ESN Mesa activities as possible. Have beers in the beer garden, go on day-trips or even longer weekend trips to Berlin or Vienna when offered. Sign up as soon as possible for the trips, they are very sought after!

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go skiing over the weekend if the weather allows it. There are several companies that offer day-trips including transport and ski-lift - you can even rent the skiing equipment fairly cheaply. Studenten im Schnee or Skibus München worked well for me.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: German culture is not that different compared to Danish cultute - we all love a beer, they just love great beer rather than average mass-produced pilsners. Munich also offers a range of nice cocktail bars and international dining - you do not have to eat meat and potatoes every time you dine out.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join the whatsapp or Facebook groups and arrange to meet with fellow exchange students. There are lots of green areas to hang out in and obviously a lot of great places for beers both outdoor or indoor.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I did not find any cultural differences particularly challenging.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The beer drinking culture at the local breweries accompanied by a hearty meal!

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1) The academics are not a cake-walk - prepare to be fairly challenged, in particular in the master progamme courses.
2) Cost of living is unfortunately quite expensive in Munich, so prepare to pay a sizable amount even for a shared flat.
3) Don't stay in the city every weekend. Make use of the opportunities to go travelling, enjoying the nature just an hour or two away.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Get a bike - especially if you live fairly centrally! Either buy one second hand which you can then sell once your semester is over or sign up for Swapfiets.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Finally "learning" how to ski

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The pandemic was obsiously a challenge. All bars/clubs ended up closing and all academic activities took place form home.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
